## Introduction

We are interested in adding more datasets to the Treehouse Splice Compendium prior to submitting the manuscript to a journal. Currently, the priorities are to include samples in the Treehouse PolyA compendia, with healthy comparators from dGTEx.

This notebook reads in the clinical metadata from the v25 Treehouse PolyA Compendium and filters for samples to download to process for the Treehouse Splice Compendium. The input files to this notebook are:

**polya_clinical_file**: [Treehouse PolyA Compendium v25 clinical metadata](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE294351), which contains clinical (disease, age at dx, sample source) information associated with a unique `th_dataset_id`. This file has more samples than recorded in `treehouse_files_on_aws`, because Treehouse does not keep all of the TARGET files processed in the PolyA compendium on AWS.

**treehouse_files_on_aws**: An internal log of sequence files in Treehouse storage. Fields consist of date, time, bytes, and path. Treehouse IDs for associating files with those in the PolyA compendium are within the values for `path`.

**TH_dataset_ID_by_collaborator_THIDs.tsv**: Internal Treehouse key of what collaborators are associated with specific Treehouse dataset IDs

**41698_2025_852_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx**: Supplementary data table 1 from [Vasquez et al. 2025](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11928651/#sec29) listing Treehouse sample IDs of 33 samples used in study.

**JAMA_TH_IDs.tsv**: Space-separated file of 144 sample IDs used in [Vaske et al. 2019](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2753519), pasted from eTable 3b in the paper's [supplement](https://cdn.jamanetwork.com/ama/content_public/journal/jamanetworkopen/938206/zoi190533supp1_prod.pdf?Expires=1794613443&Signature=WLyr7rwB8MKSlrxifyxwoJ75UMi1ByrZUUi2X~k3JhloUTzZvJTDuBzkgS8mHOvixSNDp6kPS5ygqHaNk-EcwPNC6G9mG0VXY5ORDMVdrSlCGy2WujAvboi0lCObb3GEtNBXy0iuBOKPERC3FFQX7LI4xHPxm060Gzu3ColP91exQVd1w10XJYGA6cnn5GhqMCzpC~YBCPtalUlWqaGGmKaYzaUmDCWeTDN5W0~X~VsX8yZSHS8rbj18EciADgJdPawWGDI3ml0WGrgcgbD8V2tkG33t1DcE7gJwHJLogU9PfHYNvye8TOppM8lMbcZXSt40Npr7S~XfDFvv5XA4GQ__&Key-Pair-Id=APKAIE5G5CRDK6RD3PGA). This file is not directly used as input, but is used to derive `JAMA_TH_ID_column.txt`, which is read in.

**JAMA_TH_ID_column.txt:** This file contains a column of JAMA Treehouse sample IDs and is obtained from the above file through the following command:

```         
awk 'NR > 1 {print $1}' JAMA_TH_IDs.tsv > JAMA_TH_ID_column.txt
```

**Jama_REDCap_Donor_Sample_20260730.tsv**: REDCap record of JAMA samples in Treehouse's internal database, with MEND QC information.

**Notebook output:**

This notebook produces summary tables of samples of interest from the Treehouse PolyA Compendium and samples from the Vaske 2019 and Vasquez 2025 papers.

This notebook produces output files of accession IDs of Treehouse PolyA Compendium v25 files. One output file is created for each data source (e.g. SRA, TARGET, individual collaborators). Accessions from these files will be used as input for downstream downloading scripts.

## Setup

Files and directories

```{r files_and_directories}
## Directories ##
repo_root <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::is_git_root)
metadata_dir <- file.path(repo_root, "metadata")

## Files ##
# Treehouse polyA compendium metadata file (contains disease type of samples and treehouse ID)
polya_clinical_file <- file.path(metadata_dir, "GSE294351_clinical_Treehouse-Tumor-Compendium-25.01-PolyA_20250131v1.tsv")
# record of files on AWS, with file type, path, and file size to be associated with polya_clinical_file by treehouse ID
treehouse_aws_summary_file <- file.path(metadata_dir, "archived_files_on_archive-treehouse-ucsc-edu_primary.txt")
# file associating Treehouse IDs with the name of its Treehouse partner contributor
thid_partner_file <- file.path(metadata_dir, "TH_dataset_ID_by_collaborator_THIDs.tsv")
# Treehouse IDs of files in the JAMA (Vaske 2019) and CKCC2 (Vasquez 2025) papers
jama_sample_id_file <- file.path(metadata_dir, "JAMA_TH_ID_column.txt")
vasquez_sample_id_file <- file.path(metadata_dir, "41698_2025_852_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx")
# REDCap metadata of JAMA samples, with MEND QC and library selection information
jama_redcap_file <- file.path(metadata_dir, "jama_REDCap_Donor_Sample_20260730.tsv")

# output accessions 
# accessions of polyA compendium files from public datasets to download, one file per data source
sra_accessions <- file.path(metadata_dir, "sra_polya_compendium_accessions.txt")
ega_accessions <- file.path(metadata_dir, "ega_polya_compendium_accessions.txt")
cbtn_accessions <- file.path(metadata_dir, "cbtn_polya_compendium_accessions.txt")

# accessions of Treehouse samples to download (generated by Treehouse or collaborators)
# these files should only have treehouse IDs rather than "accession" IDs
treehouse_collaborator_ids <-file.path(metadata_dir, "collaborator_polya_compendium_ids.txt")
publication_only_th_collaborator_ids <- file.path(metadata_dir, "pub_only_collaborator_ids.txt")
jama_samples_by_collaborator <- file.path(metadata_dir, "jama_samples_by_collaborator_count.txt")

```

Read in files

```{r}
## Read in files ##
# age_at_dx have "unknown" when age is unknown so coltype must be a character
polya_metadata_df <- readr::read_tsv(polya_clinical_file,
                                     col_types = readr::cols(
                                       .default = "c"
                                     ))

# internal Treehouse AWS log of files in storage, alongside file size
# this file is separated by spaces
treehouse_aws_df <- read.table(
  treehouse_aws_summary_file,
  sep = "", 
  header = FALSE, 
  col.names = c(
    "date",
    "time",
    "bytes",
    "path"),
  colClasses = c(
    bytes = "double"
  )
  )

# file associating TH dataset ID to collaboration partner
th_dataset_id_partner_df <- readr::read_tsv(thid_partner_file)

# vector of treehouse sample IDs in JAMA / Vaske 2019 publiation
jama_sample_vector <- readLines(
  jama_sample_id_file
) |>
  unique()

# vector of treehouse sample IDs in CCK2 / Vasquez 2025 publiation
vasquez_sample_vector <- readxl::read_xlsx(vasquez_sample_id_file) |>
  dplyr::pull(`Patient ID`)

# list of JAMA samples on redcap 
jama_redcap_data <- readr::read_tsv(
  jama_redcap_file,
  col_types = readr::cols_only(
    th_donor_id = "c", 
    site_id = "c",
    th_sampleid = "c",
    qc = "n",
    umend = "n",
    # polyA samples are denoted with a value of "10" here
    inv10_ribod  = "n")
  )
  
```
## Summary of JAMA and CKCC2 samples within Treehouse PolyA Compendium



Note: JAMA sample IDs are sample IDs (`TH01_0054_S01`), while CKCC2 IDs are patient IDs (`TH34_1149`), which can be derived from the sample ID column in the PolyA metadata file.

Out of all JAMA samples, check how many have no QC data (assume they are not in polyA compendium for this reason)

samples pass MEND QC if they have \>= 10M MEND reads : "The RNA-Seq data must contain at least 10 million mapped exonic, non-duplicate (MEND) reads." [(Beale 2025)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-025-05376-z)

```{r}
jama_redcap_data |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pass_mend =
    dplyr::case_when(
      umend > 10000000 ~ TRUE,
      umend < 10000000 ~ FALSE
    )
    )|>
  dplyr::summarise(.by = c(qc, pass_mend, inv10_ribod),
                   n = dplyr::n())
```

88/144 samples pass MEND QC and are polyA, so I should expect to see 88 JAMA samples in the polyA compendium.

Extract MEND-QC-pass samples in a vector

```{r}
jamna_mend_qc_pass_ids <-  jama_redcap_data |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pass_mend =
      dplyr::case_when(
        umend > 10000000 ~ TRUE,
        umend < 10000000 ~ FALSE
      )
  )|>
  dplyr::filter(
    pass_mend == TRUE
  ) |>
  dplyr::pull(th_sampleid)
```

## Clean and merge Treehouse sequence metadata

Split "path" column in AWS file into filetype and Treehouse ID fields

Filetypes in Treehouse storage are: .sra, .sra.vdbcache, sequence.txt.gz, markdown.txt, .fastq, .fq.gz, and .bam. .bam files processed by Treehouse should contained unmapped reads.

```{r clean_aws_df}
cleaned_aws_df <- treehouse_aws_df  |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    filename = basename(path),
    suffix = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(filename, "fastq") ~ "fastq",
      stringr::str_detect(filename, "fq.gz") ~ "fastq",
      stringr::str_detect(filename, "bam") ~ "bam",
      stringr::str_detect(filename, "sra") ~ "sra",
      stringr::str_detect(filename, "swp") ~ "swp",
      stringr::str_detect(filename, "txt") ~ "txt"
    ),
    th_dataset_id = stringr::str_split_i(path, "/", 3)
  )
```

Merge treehouse polyA compendium metadata with aws file information to associate file size with compendium samples. This information will be used to inform download batching strategy and estimate AWS file transfer costs.

```{r merge_compendium_with_aws}
merged_compendium_aws_df <- polya_metadata_df |> 
  dplyr::left_join(cleaned_aws_df,
                   by = "th_dataset_id") |>
  # select relevant columns for downstream filtering and summary of samples
  dplyr::select(
    th_dataset_id,
    study_id,
    age_at_dx,
    disease,
    organism,
    sex,
    study_accession,
    study_dataset_id,
    source_name,
    bytes,
    suffix
  ) |>
  # turn bytes column back into double for summing later on
  dplyr::mutate(
    bytes = as.double(bytes),
    # derive treehouse patient id from sample id by splitting on the second underscore
    th_patient_id = stringr::str_split_i(th_dataset_id, "(?<=^[^_]{1,100}_[^_]{0,100})_", 1),
    # label IDs based off if they come from JAMA or CKCC2 paper
    publication_origin = dplyr::case_when(
      th_patient_id %in% vasquez_sample_vector ~ "ckcc2_vasquez_2025",
      th_dataset_id %in% jama_sample_vector ~ "jama_vaske_2019"
    )
  )
```

Filter samples prior to summarizing. For now, I will exclude samples from TARGET and TCGA, since these are datasets not unique to Treehouse. TARGET is in Splice Compendium v1, and TCGA is primarily composed of adult samples. We could consider downloading more of TARGET (e.g. osteosarcomas) that were not downloaded previously for Splice Compendium v1.

At this stage, I will not filter for pedaya, as some samples have inconsistently annotated pedaya and/or age_at_dx (some samples with pedaya age_at_dx are labeled "unknown" pedaya and some samples have "unknown" age_at_dx but I assume are pediatric based off the study area of collaborators where samples are from

```{r filter_compendium_df}
filtered_compendium_aws_df <- merged_compendium_aws_df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    # exclude TARGET and TCGA for now
    ! source_name %in% c("TARGET", "TCGA"),
    # sanity check - some aws files are dummies with 0 bytes
    bytes > 0
  )
```

## Summarize filtered data

937 files pass the above filters. The below summary tables will provide information on the sex/disease type breakdowns of the filtered samples, how many files originate from what data source, and the file size of each file categorized by data source.

sex/disease breakdown of filtered polyA compendium files

```{r }
#| label: tbl-polya_v25_top_samples
#| tbl-cap: "Top 6 sex/disease categories with the most files"

filtered_compendium_aws_df |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    .by = c(disease, sex),
    n_samples = dplyr::n()
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(desc(n_samples)) |>
  # there are 101 rows, so print head for ease of viewing
  head()

```

Much of the compendium is composed of unusual sarcomas (n = 1 or n \< 5). The majority of the compendium after these filters consist of medulloblastoma, osteosarcoma, glioma, and Ewing's sarcoma.

Print summary of files by data source and total bytes

There are some cases where the same Treehouse sample ID appears multiple times, but the bytes are different. These are cases where multiple fastq pairs are associated with the same sample.\
The strategy for processing these files is to concatenate the fastqs into a single read1 / read2 pair, prior to trimming and alignment.

```{r data_source_file}
#| label: tbl-polya_v25_source_filesize_summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary of polyA v25 compendium files, by data source and avg bytes per file"

filtered_compendium_aws_df |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    .by = source_name,
    n_datasets = length(unique(th_dataset_id)),
    total_bytes = sum(bytes)
  )

```

\~1.8TB of data should be accessible on SRA. Some of these files are listed as .sra in glacier, so the estimated filesize may be smaller than the zipped fastqs. This group represents data that I can try downloading now, since we have sra-toolkit in our pixi environment.

"unavailable" indicates the data originate from individual collaborators, such as collaborators. These files should be downloadable on glacier, but the sequence files may need to be deposited in a repository prior to publication of their splice values.

## Summarize sequence files originating from individual collaborators

Merge filtered polyA compendium dataframe with information mapping treehouse ID to collaborator

```{r merge_with_collaborator_info}
# merge filtered compendium df with file info from aws with supplement labeling individual collaborator source of Treehouse IDs

collaborator_source_compendium_df <- filtered_compendium_aws_df |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    th_dataset_id_partner_df,
    by = c("study_id" = "TH_ID"))
```

Count number of files (multiple per patient) and samples from individual collaborators

```{r summarize_collaborator_files}
#| label: tbl-polya_v25_individual_collaborator_files
#| tbl-cap: "Number of files in the polyA v25 compendium from each individual collaborator"

# summarize data by partner they are from
collaborator_source_compendium_df |>
  # filter for samples from collaborators only
  dplyr::filter(source_name == "unavailable") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    .by = c(partner),
    n_samples = length(unique(th_dataset_id))
  )

```

In total, we have sequences from 193 samples originating from individual collaborators. 36/34 expected samples are from the CKCC2 study, while only 3/113 expected samples are from the JAMA study.

```{r}
collaborator_source_compendium_df |>
  # filter for samples from collaborators only
  dplyr::filter(source_name == "unavailable") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    .by = disease,
    n_samples = length(unique(th_dataset_id))
  ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(n_samples) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sum = sum(n_samples))
```

Count number of individual patients whose data come from individual collaborators

```{r summarize_collaborator_patients}
#| label: tbl-polya_v25_individual_collaborator_patients
#| tbl-cap: "Number of unique patients in the polyA v25 compendium from each individual collaborator"

# summarize number of unique patients whose samples are from collaborators
collaborator_source_compendium_df |>  
  # filter for samples from collaborators only
  dplyr::filter(source_name == "unavailable") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    .by = c(publication_origin, `partner`),
    # note: some samples come from the same patient
    n_patients = length(unique(th_patient_id))
  )
```

Create a table of collaborator origin of JAMA samples not in polyA compendium. These are likely collaborators we need to reach out to to request for data to be deposited.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-jama_by_collaborator_source
#| tbl-cap: "Number of JAMA samples broken down by collaborator"

jama_samples_by_collaborator_df <- dplyr::tibble(jama_sample_vector) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    TH_ID = stringr::str_split_i(jama_sample_vector, "_", 1)
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    th_dataset_id_partner_df
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    .by = c(partner, TH_ID),
    n_samples = dplyr::n()
  )

jama_samples_by_collaborator_df
```

Most of these samples are not in the PolyA compendium for a mixture of reasons

CHOC are all ribo-deplete and BC-POC fastqs cannot be accessed

Double check from REDCap data which of these samples are ribo-D (potentially a third table) – an additional column to this summary as well as another column on how many samples pass MEND QC

## Summarize samples from published data sources

```{r}
merged_compendium_aws_df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    source_name %in% c("TARGET", "CBTN")
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    .by = c(source_name, disease),
    n = dplyr::n()
  )
```

## Output a list of file accessions per data source

My assumption is that I will need a separate download script for each different data source (or at least go through a different system to download the data).

```{r write_accessions_output}

# prep filtered df for exporting file accessions
for_export_compendium_df <- collaborator_source_compendium_df |>
  dplyr::select(
    th_dataset_id,
    study_id,
    th_patient_id,
    publication_origin,
    partner,
    study_accession,
    study_dataset_id,
    source_name
  )

# export accessions lists to output
sra_df <- for_export_compendium_df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    source_name == "Sequence Read Archive"
  ) |>
  readr::write_tsv(sra_accessions)

for_export_compendium_df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    source_name == "EGA"
  ) |>
  readr::write_tsv(ega_accessions)

for_export_compendium_df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    source_name == "CBTN"
  ) |>
  readr::write_tsv(cbtn_accessions)

for_export_compendium_df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    source_name == "unavailable"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(publication_origin) |>
  readr::write_tsv(treehouse_collaborator_ids)

for_export_compendium_df |>
  dplyr::filter(
    source_name == "unavailable",
    !is.na(publication_origin)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(publication_origin) |>
  readr::write_tsv(publication_only_th_collaborator_ids)

jama_samples_by_collaborator_df |>
  readr::write_tsv(jama_samples_by_collaborator)

```
